sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by anti-HA antibody staining (cell-surface ELISA/flow); full-length HA-OX2R used as the functional reference for signaling assays. Truncation mutants showed ~29% reduced surface expression relative to HA-OX2R, implying HA-OX2R itself traffics and signals normally.
sites.rationale: OX2R is a class A GPCR with no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–51 extracellular and TM1 beginning at residue 52. The N-terminus is therefore the sole extracellular terminus available for a prepend tag, making insert_after_residue=0 the unique topology-derived junction. The paper names no specific residue, only 'the N-terminus', so position_evidence is topology_derived. Python confirms residue 1 is M and residue 51 (K) is ≥3 residues from TM1 boundary (residue 52), satisfying the distance constraint. Full-length HA-OX2R is used as the signaling and surface-expression reference throughout the study, supporting surface_and_function validation. Full-length OX2R (HCRTR2) was expressed as a membrane-anchored construct with an HA epitope tag (YPYDVPDYA) inserted at the N-terminus by PCR, in pcDNA3.1. The construct was used to assess both surface expression and signaling in transfected cells. Full-length HA-OX2R served as the positive-control reference against which C-terminal truncation mutants were compared.

sources.claim: To generate HA-tagged OX2R fragments, the sequence encoding the HA epitope tag (YPYDVPDYA) was inserted into the pcDNA3.1-OX2R and the 3 truncated C-terminal OX2R constructs at the N-terminus by polymerase chain reaction.

literature_notes: Three ledger lines were evaluated. L1 is the primary qualifying line: a full-length, membrane-anchored HA-tagged OX2R construct with the tag at the extracellular N-terminus, used for both surface and signaling assays. L2 (western blot confirmation of expression) adds no independent positional information beyond L1. L3 describes C-terminal truncation mutants (HA-M1, HA-M2) that show reduced surface expression; these truncations begin in the intracellular C-terminal tail (residues 369–444 per topology landmarks) and are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for HCRTR2. No signal peptide is present in OX2R (UniProt P41976), so the N-terminal tag is not at risk of being cleaved.

literature_other_positions.note: Start of the 76-aa C-terminal deletion in HA-M1 (residues 369–444); this region is intracellular per topology landmarks (368–444 intracellular), and its deletion reduced surface expression by ~28.73% relative to full-length HA-OX2R.

Start of the 60-aa C-terminal deletion in HA-M2 (residues 385–444); this region is intracellular per topology landmarks, and its deletion reduced surface expression by ~29.51% relative to full-length HA-OX2R.
